props.title: What Is Cupping Therapy?
props.text: Cupping is a traditional technique in which cups are placed on the skin to create suction. At Spa Bali Moon your therapist places solid cups on your back and shoulders and draws the air out with a small hand pump, so there is no flame or heat. The suction lifts the skin and the muscle beneath it, a deep, pulling feeling that many guests find relaxing. For wet cupping, your therapist makes a few tiny pricks in the skin with a sterile, single-use lancet, then the same cups draw out a little blood.

props.subTitle: Frequently Asked Questions
props.title: About Cupping Therapy in Seminyak

items.question: What is cupping therapy?
items.answer: Cupping is a traditional technique in which cups are placed on the skin to create suction. At Spa Bali Moon in Seminyak your therapist places solid cups on your back and shoulders and draws the air out with a small hand pump. The suction lifts the skin and the muscle beneath it, which feels like a deep, pulling stretch. You can choose dry cupping, with suction only, or wet cupping, which also draws out a little blood.

items.question: What is the difference between dry and wet cupping?
items.answer: Dry cupping uses suction only, and nothing breaks the skin. For wet cupping, your therapist makes a few tiny pricks in the skin with a sterile, single-use lancet, then the same hand-pump cups draw out a little blood. Here, 30 minutes of dry cupping costs IDR 499.000 and 30 minutes of wet cupping IDR 649.000 per person.

items.question: Does cupping hurt?
items.answer: Most guests describe a strong pulling feeling rather than pain. Your therapist controls the suction with the hand pump, so tell them at any time if you would like it lighter.

items.question: Will cupping leave marks?
items.answer: Often, yes. Cupping can leave round, pink to dark purple marks where the cups were placed. They are not painful and usually fade within a few days to a week, so plan around any beach photos or special events. Wet cupping also leaves the tiny pricks, which usually heal within a few days.

items.question: Do you use fire or heat?
items.answer: No. Spa Bali Moon uses solid cups with a small hand pump to draw out the air, for dry and wet cupping alike, so there is no flame, no heat and no hot glass on your skin.

items.question: Can I combine cupping with a massage?
items.answer: Yes. Book 1 hour of Balinese massage with 30 minutes of dry cupping for IDR 599.000 per person, less than the IDR 658.000 the two cost when booked separately.

items.question: How much does cupping cost in Seminyak?
items.answer: Cupping therapy at Spa Bali Moon in Seminyak costs IDR 499.000 for 30 minutes of dry cupping or IDR 649.000 for 30 minutes of wet cupping per person, or IDR 599.000 for 1 hour of Balinese massage plus 30 minutes of dry cupping. Home service at your villa or hotel adds IDR 75.000 per therapist in the Seminyak area. You can pay by Visa, Mastercard or cash, and book on WhatsApp, 9am to 11pm daily.

items.question: Can I have cupping at my villa or hotel?
items.answer: Yes. Spa Bali Moon offers dry and wet cupping as home service at villas and hotels in Seminyak and nearby areas; your therapist brings the cups, the pump, fresh linen and everything else the session needs. Home service adds IDR 75.000 per therapist in the Seminyak area.

items.question: Is cupping suitable for everyone?
items.answer: Not always. Tell us when you book if you are pregnant, take blood-thinning medication, or have sensitive, sunburnt or broken skin, so we can let you know whether cupping is right for you. This matters most for wet cupping, which draws a little blood.

items.question: Can I ask for a female or male therapist for cupping?
items.answer: Yes. Tell us your preference when you book your cupping session on WhatsApp and we'll arrange a female or male therapist, at our Seminyak spa or at your villa or hotel.
